data.description:
## The decision

**The operator has adopted option (a) of bug `f850-674c-c89f-4b97` (`unsuited-locustal-incatern`):
Windows IS now a declared support target for rebar.**

That converts `sweep (windows)` from "a permanently-red job that is not a health signal" into a
**known-incomplete support target being driven to green**. The job has never passed since it was
added by `7024c35790bc` (2026-08-26); there is no onset boundary, nothing regressed. The sweep
simply revealed that rebar does not run on Windows. This epic is the sustained commitment to make
it run.

The decision, its reasoning, and the obligations it creates on future work are recorded in an ADR
(drafted as `docs/adr/0117-windows-declared-support-target.md`); this epic is the execution vehicle.

## Scope, from measured evidence

Source: job `100874330553` of run `33824556786`, whose final line is
`510 failed, 5140 passed, 69 skipped, 206 warnings, 74 errors in 662.75s`. The log was re-read for
this decomposition rather than trusted from the bug's summary; 584 `FAILED`/`ERROR` lines across
**110 distinct test files** (510 failures + 74 collection/setup errors).

Failure-class census (counts are `E ` assertion/exception lines in that log, so they over- and
under-count individual tests slightly; they are for ORDERING, not for a burn-down target):

| Class | Evidence | Child |
|---|---|---|
| `fcntl` unguarded use in `_store/lock.py` | 384 `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'flock'` + 4 `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'fcntl'` | S1 — **gates everything** |
| Network guard leaks on Windows | 47 `RuntimeError: Network access is forbidden in unit/scripts tests` | S2 |
| POSIX mode-bit / permission assertions | 17 `CleanupError: artifact directory must not be group/world accessible`, plus `st_mode`/`chmod(0o755)` sites | S3 |
| Path-separator string semantics | 217 backslashed-path occurrences; e.g. `assert 'src/rebar/live.py:1' in '…src\rebar\live.py:1…'` | S4 |
| `os.path.relpath` across drive letters | 2 `ValueError: path is on mount 'C:', start on mount 'D:'` | S5 |
| CRLF newline translation | `assert b'{\r\n  "bin…' == b'{\n  "bindi…'` | S6 |
| cp1252 / charmap console codec | 5 `UnicodeDecodeError: 'charmap' codec can't decode byte 0x8f`, 2 `'utf-8' codec can't decode byte 0x97` | S7 |
| Windows mandatory file locking on unlink/rename | 7 `PermissionError [WinError 32] … used by another process` / `[WinError 5] Access is denied` | S8 |
| POSIX exec and signal semantics | 3 `OSError [WinError 193] %1 is not a valid Win32 application`; "a signal kill … surfaced as a POSITIVE returncode"; `.sh`-dependent gate tests | S9 |

## The ordering is not negotiable — `lock.py` FIRST

`src/rebar/_store/lock.py` accounts for roughly **74% of the failures on its own** and gates every
other class: every store write reaches `_acquire_once` → `_acquire_fcntl` (`lock.py:491`), so on
Windows every ticket write raises `AttributeError`. Until that is fixed, the other classes cannot
even be measured — their tests fail on store setup before reaching the semantics under test.

Concretely: the bug's own class list named ".EXE console-script invocation" as an independent
class. Re-reading the log shows those failures are
`subprocess.CalledProcessError: Command '…\.venv\Scripts\rebar.EXE' 'create' 'task' …` whose
captured stderr is the `flock` `AttributeError`. They are **downstream of S1, not a separate
class**, and are expected to clear when S1 lands. That is exactly why S1 must be first and why the
remaining class sizes are estimates until it is green.

**S1 therefore `blocks` every other child.** Do not work S2–S9 in parallel with S1.

## Do NOT flip `sweep (windows)` to gating on day one

Making the job voting now would redden **every** change with 510 failures that have nothing to do
with the change under review. That destroys the `Verified` signal rather than improving it — the
precise failure mode ADR 0114 exists to prevent.

The gating flip is the **last** child (S11) and is the criterion that proves this epic is done.
Until then the job stays `continue-on-error: true` — but its meaning changes from "ignorable" to
"tracked and being driven to green", and that change of meaning must be visible in the tree, which
is what S10 does.

Per **ADR 0114**, the eventual flip is itself a two-step rollout: the job must show at least one
passing run on `main` independent of the required `Verified` hot path before a later, separate
change promotes it into the aggregate in `.github/workflows/gerrit-verify.yaml`.

## The comment in `test.yml` is now FALSE

`.github/workflows/test.yml:340-344` reads:

> Non-blocking: Windows is not yet a declared support target, so a genuine incompatibility is a
> visible finding, never a red gate.

Under this decision that sentence is untrue. It is corrected by **S10**, which is unblocked and can
land immediately — it costs nothing and stops the tree from asserting the opposite of the decision
while the epic runs.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Every child S1–S9 is closed with its own named proving command passing on `windows-latest`.
2. `sweep (windows)` reports `0 failed, 0 errors` on a scheduled or dispatched run of `main`.
3. `.github/workflows/test.yml` contains no statement that Windows is not a support target.
4. `sweep (windows)` (or its successor gating job) is in the `Verified` aggregate, promoted per
   ADR 0114 with the prior independent green `main` run cited in the promotion change.
5. No child weakens the `fcntl_held=True` precondition in `_acquire_mkdir` (`lock.py:325-362`)
   without replacing the exclusivity proof it depends on, and a test fails if that invariant is
   degraded. (This is AC5 of `f850-674c-c89f-4b97`, carried forward unchanged.)

## Proving command for the epic as a whole

```
gh workflow run test.yml --ref main && \
  gh run watch --exit-status   # sweep (windows) must report 0 failed, 0 errors
```
data.title: Windows portability: drive the declared Windows support target from 510 sweep failures to a gating green job
